problem: Prior large-scale RL visual navigation relies on GPS as ground truth for image labeling and end-to-end raw-image training, which is hard to train and fails when GPS is poor or absent across month-spaced traversals with extreme visual change.
motivation: Real-world navigation arises from both motion and local visual perception, yet motion estimation (VO, SLAM, radar) and vision (VPR) are usually used separately. GPS in large driving datasets like Oxford RobotCar is unreliable across traversals, so vision-only RL agents that depend on it break down.
key_idea: Temporally fuse compact NetVLAD image descriptors (64-d) with compact 2-d motion estimates (GPS, VO or radar odometry) as the state for a PPO-trained LSTM navigation policy in the CityLearn environment.
insight: Adding precise motion input lets the agent avoid dependence on noisy GPS labels. On Oxford 'clouds' (no GPS), MVP-RO reaches 93% success versus 7% for vision-only, and MVP-VO reaches 53%. A trade-off curve shows RL success rises as VO precision improves, so motion quality directly limits navigation performance.
method: Compact visual representation: off-the-shelf NetVLAD (VGG-16, PCA+whitening) encodes RGB images into 64-d descriptors x_t
Motion representation: 2-d motion m_t from raw GPS, visual odometry, or optimized radar odometry (Oxford Radar RobotCar); Nordland uses GPS only
Bimodal state: m_t and x_t are combined into a compact b_t, with the goal also encoded as a 2-d vector g_t
Policy network: a linear 512-unit layer on b_t, then a 256-unit LSTM together with the previous action, with policy and value heads, trained with PPO
Reward and curriculum: sparse +1 reward on reaching the target, with multi-level curriculum learning in the CityLearn environment
Baseline: Mirowski-style vision-only agent with a 2-layer CNN on 84x84 raw images that uses GPS labels

setting.backbone: NetVLAD (frozen, off-the-shelf) + linear/LSTM PPO policy (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Single traversal of Oxford RobotCar or Nordland Railway in CityLearn (real driving images + motion data); no extra data
setting.observation: 64-d NetVLAD image descriptors + 2-d odometry/GPS motion + 2-d goal vector
setting.simulator: CityLearn (built on real Oxford RobotCar and Nordland datasets)
setting.privileged: none (motion from GPS/VO/radar odometry as sensor input; GPS used for image labeling in the vision-only baseline)

numbers.eval_set_note: 'clouds' traversal (no GPS data); average over 10 deployment iterations with 100 targets each
numbers.backbone: NetVLAD 64-d + LSTM PPO, optimized radar odometry
numbers.extra: radar odometry ground truth from Oxford Radar RobotCar
numbers.evidence: the MVP-RO agent achieves 93% success rate under clouds conditions, with no GPS data available, compared to 7% for the vision only agent
Abstract: MVP can achieve 53% and 93% navigation success rate using VO and RO, respectively, compared to 7% for a vision-only method

numbers.eval_set_note: winter traversal; approximate value read from figure text
numbers.backbone: NetVLAD 64-d + LSTM PPO, raw GPS motion
numbers.evidence: vision only agent achieves around 86% success rate under winter, compared to around 94% for the MVP-GPS agent

numbers_note: Results are mostly in bar charts (Figs. 2, 8); only the numbers quoted in the text are captured. The Nordland value is stated as 'around'. This is not a standard VLN benchmark.
results: On Oxford RobotCar 'clouds' with no GPS, MVP-RO gets 93% and MVP-VO 53% success versus 7% for the vision-only agent. On Nordland winter, MVP-GPS gets about 94% versus about 86%. MVP is consistently robust across all weather traversals, while vision-only fails under poor GPS.
limitations: Evaluated only on replayed real-data traversals (CityLearn) with a discrete action space, not on a real robot or with free-form navigation
Depends on the quality of the motion estimate; VO needs scale handling and the motion encoding is only 2-d
Trained per traversal on a single route; the vision-only baseline is a weak, simplified raw-image agent
builds_on: Mirowski et al. 2018 (learning to navigate in cities without a map)
compares_to: Vision-only RL agent (Mirowski et al. 2018 style)
